title: Renewal & expansion check-in - Solaris Tech
next_steps: Maya to send updated pricing for 3x dedicated pool expansion and EU region add-on by 2027-06-20
Devon to run a 2-hour benchmark for Solaris dev dataset on 8xA100 config and share results by 2027-06-22
Lena to schedule an executive summary call w/ procurement and legal next week
action_items: Maya Chen - send updated contract amendment & pricing for capacity increase - 2027-06-20
Devon Patel - run benchmarking on 8xA100 + q4 quant profile and share logs - 2027-06-22
Jordan Lee - provide compliance contact for KMS/HSM questions - 2027-06-21
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in. Solaris wants to extend contract 12 months, upgrade dedicated capacity from 4 GPUs to 12 GPUs (staged), and add EU region. Key concerns: data residency, KMS integration, cost/latency tradeoffs, and SLA during rollout. Redwood to provide updated pricing & benchmark results; follow-up legal/procurement call scheduled.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, Devon (SE) and Lena (CSM) are with me. How are you all?
[00:08] Alex Romero: Good, thanks. Quick background - we put Redwood in production in Q4 last year, running inference for chat and reranking, currently on a 4-GPU dedicated pool in us-west.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Yep, and we are hitting throughput cap during peak, especially for long-context chat, so looking at capacity upgrade.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Great, that's the reason for today's renewal + expansion check-in. We saw usage ramp and the renewal is up in July. Wanted to align on timeline and options: staged capacity increase, adding EU region for data residency, and contract extension.
[00:41] Sam Wallace: From procurement, timeline is pretty tight - need numbers and updated SOW for legal review by end of next week.
[00:46] Devon Patel: Quick clarifying q: what are your latency SLOs for the expanded traffic? Are you targeting p95 under 350ms for user-facing chat?
[00:54] Priya Singh: Ideally p95 < 300ms. Right now p95 is around 380ms during peak, so we want to get that down without blowing up cost.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Also want the EU region because of a EU customer pilot coming in Q4 - we need data residency and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM there.
[01:14] Maya Chen: Noted. We can propose adding an EU-dedicated pool and cross-region routing. We provide cross-region replication for KV caches but there are tradeoffs, and I want Devon to talk about batching and quantization options.
[01:24] Devon Patel: Sure - for long-context chat you can get big wins with prefix/KV cache and by switching to a 4-bit quant profile on some workloads. For example, on our benchmark last month, moving to q4 reduced GPU memory and allowed doubling effective concurrency. Note: quant can introduce small quality deltas, we should validate on your eval set.
[01:40] Priya Singh: We care about quality, so we'll want an eval harness run. Can you run it against our sample prompts?
[01:46] Devon Patel: Definitely - please share the prompt set link, or I can use the shared folder you sent earlier.
[01:51] Alex Romero: We'll share a trimmed dataset. Also, can you confirm KMS integration? We use Azure Key Vault and want HSM-backed keys.
[01:58] Lena Ortiz: We support customer-managed KMS via HSM integrations; our private deployment offers direct KMS connectors. For hosted/dedicated we have options to integrate with Azure Key Vault but we'll need the security team to sign off. I'll queue the security docs.
[02:09] Priya Singh: Cool. A couple more specifics: our current peak concurrency is about 160 reqs/min (avg 90) and our average token length is 1.2k tokens for chat.
[02:19] Devon Patel: Helpful. For 1.2k tokens with that concurrency, we'd recommend moving from your 4-GPU pool to an 8-GPU initially and then scale to 12 GPUs if the benchmarks look good. We can also add a dedicated EU pool with regional routing and origin-aware caching.
[02:33] Sam Wallace: Pricing? What's the delta per month for 8->12 GPUs and adding EU region? We need a ballpark to feed procurement.
[02:40] Maya Chen: We'll prepare a few scenarios: staged (4->8->12) and immediate (12), plus EU add-on. I'll send a spreadsheet with committed and burst pricing.
[02:48] Alex Romero: For the contract, we also want to extend for 12 months with a review at 6 months. Any early term exit terms?
[02:55] Maya Chen: Standard amendment templates include a 30-day termination clause for material breaches; for reserved capacity commits there are commit terms, but we can include a mid-term review and a flexibility clause for capacity changes. I'll have legal look at it.
[03:06] Jordan Lee: On the technical side, we'd like to schedule a deep-dive for SREs to go over autoscaling, KV cache warmup, and network egress.
[03:14] Devon Patel: Happy to run that; I can walk through autoscaling policies, burst capacity, and the cache pre-warming flow. FYI, sometimes the auto-batcher behavior leads to p95 spike if the incoming arrival pattern is bursty - we can tune batch windows and keep-liveness thresholds.
[03:28] Priya Singh: And about quality degradation with q4 - what are the rollback policies?
[03:33] Devon Patel: We have model variant rollouts with automatic fallback to fp16 or previous quant profile on quality regressions, and we tie regressions to labeled eval sets so you can revert automatically. We'll propose a canary rollout in EU first, then global.
[03:47] Alex Romero: Security checklist: SOC 2, ISO 27001? We need SOC 2 Type II and an audit log retention option of 1 year for compliance.
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and can provide certificate; audit logs available with configurable retention (add-on for 1 year). I'll attach the certs and the audit-log addon pricing.
[04:05] Sam Wallace: Legal will want indemnity language and data processing addendum, especially for EU region.
[04:11] Maya Chen: Understood, we'll include DPA and standard privacy terms. I'll loop in legal after this.
[04:16] Speaker 2: [unintelligible] - is there any impact on latency if we enable synchronous replication for KV cache across regions?
[04:22] Devon Patel: Synchronous replication adds latency; we typically recommend async replication with eventual consistency and a hot-warm cache strategy. If you need strong consistency, we can architect it but p95 will increase.
[04:32] Priya Singh: Can you share any numbers? Ballpark added latency for sync replicate?
[04:36] Devon Patel: Depends on inter-region link, but expect +40-120ms on top of base p95. That's why we usually favor regional pools and route EU traffic to EU pool.
[04:47] Maya Chen: Let's talk pilot plan: proposed timeline - sign amendment by 6/25, run benchmark 6/22, deploy EU small pool 7/10, scale main pool 7/20. Thoughts?
[04:57] Alex Romero: Tight but workable if we get pricing and SOW today or tomorrow. Procurement needs the numbers.
[05:03] Sam Wallace: If you can get a clear SOW and commitment options, we can tee up legal.
[05:07] Lena Ortiz: I'll prepare SOW templates and an executive summary for procurement.
[05:11] Priya Singh: One more question - telemetry export. Can you stream per-route traces to our Datadog?
[05:16] Devon Patel: Yes, we have tracing hooks and can push to Datadog or open-telemetry collector. There is a small egress cost for logs.
[05:23] Jordan Lee: Also want RBAC so our product teams can't change the capacity, only view.
[05:28] Maya Chen: RBAC is configurable in Console; we can set roles and tie to SSO. I'll include a role matrix.
[05:33] Alex Romero: Anything else on your side?
[05:36] Priya Singh: Could you include a rough per-token cost delta if we move to q4 quant vs fp16 and the expected throughput improvement? That will help justify quality testing.
[05:44] Devon Patel: Yes, I'll include a cost model row: estimated per-token cost drop ~30% on q4 for generation-heavy workloads, but we'll validate on your eval set.
[05:53] Maya Chen: Good. Recap of action items: Maya sends pricing & amendment, Devon runs benchmark on your sample, Lena sends security & SOW docs, Jordan provides KMS contact. Any other next steps?
[06:05] Alex Romero: We'll share prompt set and sample logs by EOD.
[06:09] Sam Wallace: Procurement to provide vendor info requirements to Maya.
[06:12] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule the SRE deep-dive.
[06:16] Speaker 2: Thanks.
[06:18] [call ends] 

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (Speaker 2 label used where name uncertain), references to shared artifacts: shared deck and pricing spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/s/solaris-q2-pricing), eval harness: https://redwood.app/evals/solaris-sample.
